title: Yet another reminder that the most exciting and daring work in NYC is...
transcript: What if I told you that the best new musical of the season is not actually playing on Broadway, but rather a tiny 300 seat off Broadway theatre? I am, of course, talking about Mexodus, which just began its off Broadway run at the Daryl Roth Theatre. And I am not exaggerating when I say I think it is better than most of the shows on Broadway right now. It shines a spotlight on an aspect of American history that really isn't taught in schools. That being the Underground Railroad that went south into Mexico, which thousands of enslaved people used to escape their captivity and to gain their freedom. And while the characters in the show are fictional, their story serves as a stand in for the thousands of true stories that never get told. The entire show is written and performed by two actors, Brian Quijada and Nygel D. Robinson. And when I say they are performing the whole show, I mean they are performing the whole show. Everything from the vocals, the music, the sound effects is being done live on stage by these two performers. And this is achieved through looping technology, where they'll play a couple of bars of music on, say, guitar or cello or beatboxing, and then they'll loop a recording of that over and over again while slowly adding more and more layers until they get a very full sound. And it is very, very cool to experience live. The score itself, Is primarily hip hop with some Spanish Latin influences seeping in. And because of that, you're going to hear the show compared to Hamilton a lot. And while I don't think that comparison is completely fair, I did have the same feeling listening to this score as I did listening to Hamilton for the first time. I was just constantly wowed and delighted by the seemingly endless creativity and lyricism on display. This is a really dense score, and while it is easy enough to follow for a first timer, it is also one of those scores that is going to reward multiple listens as you notice things that you weren't able to catch the first time. And that is not something that I have felt about a new musical score in a while.
